messages:
Alex: kicking off warmup+stress run for ap-south1 bring-up. primary goals: validate autoscaler behavior under bursty traffic, warm GPU pools, and confirm fallbacks work. schedule: today 14:00-18:30 UTC.

Maria: ETA on the load script? what's the expected qps/token/sec profile?

Alex: using our loaddriver (k6 wrapper). profile: short bursts to simulate PLG peaks: 0-5m ramp to 2000 rps, hold 10m, spike to 6k rps for 2m, back to 1k for 15m. token throughput ~ 45k tps peak.

Alex: load command to run from stress-worker pool:
```bash
./loaddriver run --profile ap-south1-warmup --workers 12 --duration 4h \n  --script ./profiles/ap-south1/spike.json \n  --out influxdb=http://metrics-collector:8086
```

Sam: autoscaler values we should test: target_token_utilization, min/max node pools, grace period. propose: target_util: 0.6, max_nodes: 120, min_nodes: 12, scale_cooldown: 60s. will push a canary config to staging first.

Jin: quick checklist for health probes before we start:
- kube-scheduler: kubectl get cs
- node readiness: kubectl get nodes -o wide
- GPU drivers: nvidia-smi on a sample node
- inference runtime health: curl -sS http://10.2.3.45:8080/health | jq

Luca: FYI ap-south1 has a strict egress cap on the trial account. we should enable request shaping to avoid hitting cloud egress burst throttle. set egress throttle to 30Mi/s on stress-workers.

deploy-bot: config-deploy:autoscaler-canary applied to cluster/ap-south1-canary by @Sam at 2026-03-18T12:45:10Z

Maria: metrics to watch (alerts):
- p50/p95 latency (generation completion)
- token-per-second (TPS) output by runtime
- GPU util per-pod (nvidia-smi exporter)
- queue_length and pending_requests
- pod OOM/killed count
- 5xx error rate > 0.5%
- node provisioning time > 5m

Alex: thresholds/rollback triggers:
- if p95 > 2s for >10m -> pause load and investigate
- if GPU util < 20% while queue_length > 100 -> sched bottleneck -> revert new kernel flags
- if 5xx > 1% for 5m -> rollback routing to fallback model pool
- if node provisioning time > 8m for 3 consecutive nodes -> abort test and scale down

Sam: ramp plan (explicit):
- 00-10m: sanity ramp to 5% traffic
- 10-30m: steady 25% (warm GPU caches)
- 30-60m: step to 60%
- 60-80m: 100% spike test (2m bursts every 10m)
- 80-200m: soak at 50% to validate autoscaler steady-state

Jin: cluster tuning notes to apply in canary if needed:
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: runtime-hpa
spec:
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 200
  metrics:
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: token_throughput
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "2500"
```

Luca: cost note: if we hold 120 nodes with 8xA100 for 2 hours we’re looking at ~ $18k raw compute (spot mix lowers it). propose reserve a small dedicated pool (12 nodes) and use spot for burst capacity. document cost delta in post-run notes.

Alex: handoff summary I'll paste to the runbook after the test. items to include: exact load command, canary config hash, observed anomalies, timeline, metric snapshots, cost delta, and next actions.

Maria: can someone own oncall for that window? also want an on-call checklist in the runbook steps.

Jin: I can be oncall for 14:00-18:30 UTC. will post contact and escalation steps in the runbook.

Alex: perfect — tagging ops: @Jin will act as primary, @Sam backup. when we start we’ll post short live updates here. please ack if you saw the plan :thumbsup:

Sam: ack :thumbsup:

Luca: ack, will watch egress and cost dashboards.

deploy-bot: loaddriver:run started by @Alex at 2026-03-18T14:00:05Z

Alex: starting first ramp now. will call out any anomalies.

Jin: oncall ack, monitoring dashboards up: https://grafana.internal/redwood/ap-south1-warmup

Maria: thanks team. leaving my phone on for alerts.

Alex: update @ 14:22 UTC — minor pod crashloop on node pool gpustage-3; restarting pods resolved it, investigating scheduler logs. not impacting latency yet.

Jin: looked at node kubelet logs, saw transient GPU driver OOM on 1 pod, marking node for cordon and reprovision.

Alex: will note that under anomalies. continuing soak.

Maria: please capture p95 and TPS snapshots at 14:30 and 15:30 for the postmortem.

Jin: ack, will export dashboards and upload to runbook after the run.

Alex: when we're done I'll push a short summary and cost numbers. thanks everyone for quick turn.
